- Tip rot (brown/necrotic tissue at tip)
- Pinkish/reddish discoloration on kernels
- Possible white/pinkish mold growth near the tip area

This pattern suggests Gibberella ear rot or Fusarium ear rot. Let me check reference images.

Aspergillus shows olive-green powdery mold — clearly different from the test image.

**Summary of observations:**
- Test image: corn ear, husk pulled back, pinkish/reddish kernel discoloration, brown necrotic tip rot
- Gibberella (refs 12, 42, 64): tip rot pattern, and ref 64 shows distinctive pink/purple coloration — closest match
- Fusarium (refs 25, 42): scattered kernel rot with white/gray mold, no tip-down progression — doesn't match
- Diplodia: tip rot but white mold, different color profile
- Trichoderma: green mold — doesn't match
- Aspergillus: olive-green powdery mold — doesn't match

The pink/reddish kernel coloration combined with tip rot is the hallmark of Gibberella ear rot (caused by *Fusarium graminearum*), which produces characteristic pink-red pigmentation starting from the tip.
